rationale_bullets: Lindsey's redshirt-freshman baseline: 70.5 PFF/440 dropbacks (B10 +1 -> 71.5, ~p49), 2,382 @ 63%, 18-6 - '#11 in the Big Ten in QB Rating, tied with fellow freshman Bryce Underwood' (P6).
Ball-security and late-game evidence: six INTs all year; game-winning drives to beat Rutgers and Michigan State; Fleck - 'took really good command of the offense.'
Second-year program is named and specific (P6): pre-snap reads, audibles, pocket elusiveness; 'should get a second-year bonus.'
The ceiling caveat: the offense around him ranked #131 in long-passing explosiveness (P6) - the tape is command-over-splash.
58, M = two ticks under the Washington/Underwood 60 tier: same tape zone, full staff continuity, less pedigree heat.
data_gaps: No dated spring reporting beyond books

rationale_bullets: Taylor is proven at rate: 77.5 PFF/143 att (at the p52 RB reference), 670 @ 5.6 in an injury-shortened year, 986 in 2024, back-to-back 100s to close; 'the offense was noticeably different with him in the backfield' (P6).
The health file is the cap: ~5 games missed in 2025, an IFS stretch as a freshman; Athlon documents the offseason body work (chef, Pilates).
Depth is names-plus-hints: Turner (77.7/16; 864 @ 8.3 at Marshall in 2024, OFY wk 3), Washington (81.1/21), the Purdue swap (Thomas in, Ijeboi 75.5/98 out), FRs Estrada/Bates.
Team context: RUN 46p as-played, #116-128 ypg by book - the line and injuries share blame.
54, M = above-average: elite-adjacent rate stats on fragile volume.
Returned breadth, no proven No. 1: Tracy (68.9/315 -> 67.9; 1st-tm MAC in 2024) + Smith (62.9/230) combined 65/873/10 (P6); Athlon: 'retained its Nos. 2-4 pass-catchers.'

The imports address named problems: Steptoe (61.1/299, AAC +0) 'led the AAC in average depth of target' - the vertical fix for a #131 long-passing offense; Jennings (67.1/209, AAC) tops Athlon's add list; Thompson (52.6/226 at Auburn, SEC +6 -> 58.6) is a former FIVE-STAR whose actual tape is poor - pedigree lottery ticket, priced as priors (prompt rule 3).
GONE: Brockington (71.3/309) plus BOTH TE producers (Geers, Biber); the TE room is a print conflict (Athlon: Walsh; P6: Oklahoma transfer Helms) - battle documented.
2025 context: RECV 40th percentile.
Mechanical aggregate ~63.5 (~p32) + breadth = 44, M.
data_gaps: Whether Thompson's spring justified the 'instant impact' line

rationale_bullets: The three best tapes return: Johnson (75.1/757 -> 74.1) - PS's 1st-TEAM ALL-AMERICAN at LG - Roy (68.6/766 -> 67.6; PS#40, 'on NFL scouts radar'), Beers (64.0/759 -> 63.0), plus Nelson (62.7/197, moved up late).
The two WORST full-volume tapes leave: Ray (62.1/748) and Marshall (49.6/644) - subtraction as addition.
The books split and both are held: P6 '#123 in my OL Run Push... rebuilding the right side' vs PS 'one of the offense's strengths'; the PFF tape sides nearer PS (RBLK 74p, PBLK 57p, 24 sacks).
RT is the open spot: FR Shipp (Athlon print) vs Warren (50.3/76 at Tennessee - Top100 pedigree, poor tiny tape).
Mechanical returning aggregate ~67.8 (~p55) + the weak-link subtraction + a PS-AA anchor = 60, M.
data_gaps: Run-push vs pass-pro split under the same line returning

rationale_bullets: The edge trio is the case: A.Smith (71.6/671 -> 81.6; 1st-tm All-B10; B10-best 12.5 sacks - first double-digit Gopher season since 2009; turned down the NFL) + Menz (67.2/386 -> 77.2; 6.5 sk) + Bush (69.1/691 at Cal -> 70.1; 'Cal's best pass rusher'; 91 pressures/13 sk over three years - Athlon). P6: 'one of the best in the Big Ten.'

The interior is a stated rebuild: 'the top four defensive tackles departing' (P6) - Eastern (67.3/499) and Logan-Redding (57.4/415) headline. Replacements are G5-discounted: Crowder (76.5/317 at Marshall, SBC -6 -> 70.5; 'needs to be an anchor'), Chapman (73.9/316 at FIU, CUSA -8 -> 65.9), Kaba (72.3/154 -> 66.3).
The signal conflict is held, not averaged: 35 sacks, a 9-sack school record vs Nebraska, #4 Negative Play Rate (P6) - versus RDEF 40p / PRSH 36p as-played; the havoc clustered against bad offenses.
Howard (56.8/423 -> 66.8; Athlon returning-starter flag) deepens the rotation.
Mechanical weighted aggregate ~73.5 (~p70); interior projection risk lands it 64, M.
data_gaps: Whether the sack profile survives better OLs

rationale_bullets: Baranowski is the best returning LB tape in the B10 set so far: 77.2 PFF/667 snaps (-> 93.2 with the +16, but the raw number needs no help); All-B10; 103 tackles - the first 100-tackle Gopher season since 2018.
Behind him: Kingsbury (61.2/266 -> 77.2, #8 tackler), Karmo (59.5/156), hints in Carrier (75.7/21) and Gerlach (70.8/63). GONE: Williams (67.7/664, 12 starts).
Fleck (attributed): '6 deep at LB... a strength of the D'; the tape says one star plus ascending role players; A.Marshall (53.9/295 at EMU, MAC -12) is depth only.
LB caution: the room's non-Baranowski raws are modest; the offset does the flattering. 55, M.
data_gaps: No sub-grade extract for the caution-preferred signals

rationale_bullets: Nestor is the headline tape: 81.5 PFF/608 (B10 +6 -> 87.5) - the best returning CB grade in this conference build so far; HM All-B10; Fleck's 'ultimate competitor.' Brown (69.9/639 -> 75.9; HM All-B10) anchors safety - Athlon: 'more reliable than Perich a year ago.'

The famous departure is priced by tape, not name: Perich (to Oregon) graded 61.0 on 789 snaps in his slump year - the 2025 on-field loss is real but modest; the return-game/ceiling loss shows up in ST.
The rest is projection: A.West (62.7/381 as an MSU true FR) 'could be the starter opposite Nestor' (P6); Harden the midseason convert 'impressed'; Gousby (61.5/435); FCS wildcard M.Smith (Lehigh).
Context held: PDR #96, COV 35p as-played - the unit's names outran its 2025 tape.
Mechanical aggregate ~75.4 (~p80) is two-player-driven; CB2/NB projection pulls it to 64, M.
data_gaps: NB (Monroe 78.9/49) sample too small to trust

rationale_bullets: ST rule: start at the 99th-percentile prior SPEC, then subtract the two engines that left: K Denaberg (14-21, 2-7 from 40+ - the weakness, but still the only proven leg) and Perich's elite double-duty returns (6.7 PR / 26.3 KR).
What returns is real: P Weston (42.6/38.6 net - 'a quality first season') and LS Soukup ('Mr Reliable and an NFL prospect' - PS).
The K battle is a genuine zero: Sunderland (Michigan) vs D.Jackson - 'neither has attempted a collegiate field goal' (Athlon).
PS's STR #88 dissents from the PFF SPEC 99 (coverage/return units vs grade) - both held. 56, M.
